source.author: verg
source.text: Te Stygii tremuere lacus, te ianitor Orci ossa super recubans antro semesa cruento; nec te ullae facies, non terruit ipse Typhoeus, arduus arma tenens; non te rationis egentem Lernaeus turba capitum circumstetit anguis.
source.text_original: Te Stygii tremuere lacus, te ianitor Orci / ossa super recubans antro semesa cruento; / nec te ullae facies, non terruit ipse Typhoeus, / arduus arma tenens; non te rationis egentem / Lernaeus turba capitum circumstetit anguis.
source.text_english: At you the Stygian pools trembled, at you the doorkeeper of Orcus, reclining over his half-eaten bones in his bloody cave; nor did any shapes frighten you, not Typhoeus himself, towering as he held his weapons; nor did the Lernaean serpent, with its crowd of heads, encircle you in your lack of reason.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: sed neque bella videt Graias neque monstra per urbes ulla: Cleonaeo iam tempora clusus hiatu Alcides; olim Lernae defensus ab angue Areas, et ambobus iam cornua fracta iuvencis.
reuse.text_original: sed neque bella videt Graias neque monstra per urbes / ulla: Cleonaeo iam tempora clusus hiatu / Alcides; olim Lernae defensus ab angue / Areas, et ambobus iam cornua fracta iuvencis.
reuse.text_english: but he sees neither wars among the Greeks nor any monsters through the cities: Alcides is now shut in by the Cleonaean chasm; long ago Arcadia was defended by the serpent of Lerna, and now the horns of both bulls have been broken.
